== DETERMINISM MECHANISM (run.py, 3437 lines) ==
Contract stated at run.py:26-27 ("same seed+config -> byte-identical data"); tested at tests/test_pipeline.py:74-83 (same seed -> equal data_digest; different seed -> different).

RNG discipline, two tiers:
(1) ONE global scenario stream rng = random.Random(cfg.seed) (run.py:1416), consumed in strict event order for: report ingest delay rng.uniform(0, net_delay_max) (run.py:2079), per-message ground-truth emission sampling (2657), per-packet channel loss (2751), report_prob coins (2775, 2888, 2918). This stream is extremely order-sensitive: one extra/missing/reordered reception shifts every subsequent draw.
(2) Dozens of dedicated STRING-KEYED streams random.Random(f"{cfg.seed}:<label>[:<id>]") so opt-in features never perturb the default sequence: per-vehicle spawn params ":veh:{vid}" (1524), attack-mix pick ":atkmix:{vid}" (1536), onset jitter ":onset:{vid}" (1614), pulse phase ":pulse:{vid}" (1617), CRL-awareness ":crlaware:{vid}" (1619), flow arrivals ":flow" (1720), fixed-fleet roles ":attackers"/":faulty"/":collusion" (1756/1762/1766), VRUs ":vru:{vid}" (1650) + ":vruflow" (1788), per-vehicle sensor noise vrng ":sensor:{vid}" (1801), DENM ":denm:{vid}" (1804), flow collusion victims ":collude_victim:{vid}" (1869), fabricated evidence ":collude_fab:{vid}" (2925), MOBIL lane-change reconsideration ":lanechg:{vid}" (2387), PER-LINK radio shadowing ":shadow:{digest}:{rx.vid}:{step}" (2742-2743). Crypto material derives via cfg.derive(label)=sha256(f"{seed}|{label}") (507-508) feeding deterministic Ed25519 keypair_from_seed (scms_core/crypto_abstract.py:43-47); HashedId8 per IEEE 1609.2 (crypto_abstract.py:58-60).

Byte-identical-by-default invariants: default ATTACK_CATALOG tuple is FROZEN because the golden digest depends on its exact contents+order (run.py:48-60); opt-in families (COMBINED_ATTACKS 67-69, IDENTITY_SPOOF 84-87, DENM 97-99) are excluded from the default so the default digest never moves. Extra schema columns (station_type, detnorm_vruImpersonation, detnorm_denmPlausibility) and extra output files (ma_denm_log.jsonl, gt_denm_emissions.jsonl) are gated on feature flags (_emit_station_type 1444, _denm_enabled 1452, DET_KEYS gating 2047-2053, subclassed dataclasses _GtVehicleVru/_MaCertStatusVru 690-725, DENM files 3028-3036) so a run with a feature off is byte-identical to historic goldens. Even magnitude scaling folds into a multiplier AFTER the rng draw so draw count never changes (attack_claim comment 1904-1908, RandomSpeed 1926-1931).

Order determinism: spawn_order sorted by (spawn_time, vid) (2507); active_list iterated in sorted(active) vid order every step (2540); car-following reads a frozen start-of-step snapshot so the update is order-independent (2406-2407); reception candidates from the spatial hash are re-sorted into broadcast order before loss draws (cand.sort() 2721, comment 2686-2689); MA revocation iterates sorted(touched_subjects) (2944); gap-acceptance priority is a strict total order (dnode, vid) with no RNG (2420-2441); _weighted_pick and _parse_* re-canonicalize dict order (168, 190, 227, 230-238). Non-flow outputs are sorted by stable keys at write time (_write_outputs run.py:3059-3075: reports by (ingest_time, report_id), certs by digest, etc.); flow-mode streamed files rely on deterministic generation order instead.

Serialization: every row goes through ca.canonical_bytes = json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=True, bytes->hex) (crypto_abstract.py:28-40); files opened with encoding="utf-8", newline="\n" (2186-2188, 3052); floats rounded to 3 decimals at emission (e.g. 1582, 2139-2145, 2660-2664).

Manifest + digest: _data_digest (3102-3108) = sha256 over sorted(rel_path + per-file sha256) of DATA files only. _write_manifest (3111-3127) records dataset_version, seed, the FULL config dict (tuples->lists), schema_versions, standards_profile, data_digest_sha256, per-file sha256 list, counts; build_utc (wall clock) is in the manifest but NOT in the digest (3114). manifest.json itself, live_state.json, network.json are excluded from data_files, hence digest-safe (2209-2235: live snapshot is atomic os.replace, best-effort, "NOT part of the data digest"). Round-trip replay: config_from_dict (1364-1391) accepts a raw config or a full manifest.json, warns on unknown keys, coerces list->tuple and str->int element types; CLI --config replays a saved run byte-for-byte (3318-3328); --check-config validates without running (3302-3311); --dump-config emits the effective config (3427-3432). GUI runs the pipeline on a ThreadingHTTPServer thread (gui/server.py:19-553,1056) — the SIGINT registration tolerates non-main threads (run.py:2515-2522 catches ValueError).

== STREAMING WRITES / MEMORY BOUNDS ==
Flow mode (traffic_flow=True) streams the three big tables (ma_reports, gt_report_labels, gt_emissions_sample) to open .jsonl handles, flushed EVERY step (stream setup 2180-2188, flush_streams 2190-2200, per-step flush 2962-2963); accumulators are cleared each flush so memory is O(active fleet), not O(run length). Detection state is LRU-pruned every state_prune_every=50 steps with ttl=20 steps (prune_state 2202-2207, cfg 494-495); despawned vehicles free their history and RNG objects (2535-2539); max_total_vehicles caps spawns (1726-1727). Side files are written once at the end (_write_side_files 3078-3092). DENM logs are bounded accumulators, never streamed (3025-3036 comment). Fixed-fleet (default) mode holds everything in memory and sorts at the end (_write_outputs).

== Ctrl-C PARTIAL FINALIZE ==
SIGINT handler (2511-2522) sets _ABORT flag; loop checks it at step top and BREAKS TO THE NORMAL FINALIZATION PATH, resetting n_steps=step so the manifest reflects steps actually run (2524-2530); second Ctrl-C restores default handler and hard-aborts (2517-2519); previous handler restored after the loop (2967-2971); stream handles closed (2973-2975); manifest + digest still written. _ABORT reset per run (1415, not reentrant). PER_STEP_HOOK is the deterministic test seam (1402, tests/test_interrupt.py:10-59 verifies partial dataset has valid manifest, matching stream line counts, is featurizable, and that a stale flag never truncates the next run).

== RECORD SCHEMA (schemas/records.py) ==
Two disjoint visibility families enforced by a machine-checkable firewall: MA/"PUBLIC" rows may feed ML; ORACLE rows are labels only (records.py:22-27). FORBIDDEN_FEATURE_KEYS + is_forbidden_feature_key (records.py:33-65) define leakage (catches true_*, label_*, attack_*, *RealId camelCase, underscore-hidden variants); datagen/leakage_linter.py fails the build on violation. MA-visible dataclasses: MaEvidenceMessage (71-86), MaReport — TS 103 759-shaped, digests only, reason_codes, detector_outputs, st_bbox (89-109), MaCertStatus (112-125), MaInvestigation — identity never reaches MA, opaque resolved_case_handle (128-146), MaCrlEvent PUBLIC (149-158). Ground truth: GtVehicle (164-176), GtIdentityMap pseudonym->true id (179-189), GtAttack with attack_onset_time = first materially falsified message (192-204), GtReportLabel correctness taxonomy (207-216), GtLinkageRevocation (219-227). Plain dataclasses chosen explicitly because asdict() serialization is trivially deterministic (records.py:13-14). run.py extends rows via subclassing only under opt-in flags (run.py:683-731). NOTE: datagen/models.py is NOT a record schema — it is a dependency-free numpy histogram-GBDT baseline, deliberately RNG-free/deterministic (models.py:1-12, fit_gbdt 105-128); the actual record schema lives in schemas/records.py.

== PERFORMANCE ==
Pure scalar Python: run.py imports no numpy (30-46); math is per-vehicle Python floats; single-threaded; no multiprocessing anywhere in datagen (massive.py enumerates domains sequentially, streaming+deleting each domain dir to bound disk/memory, massive.py:21-25). No wall-clock perf figures are recorded anywhere in the repo (no benchmarks of steps/s). Complexity engineering instead: reception uses a spatial hash with cell=radio_range so it is O(active x local density) not O(active^2) (2686-2696); car-following uses cells of max(idm_lookahead,70?) _CF_CELL=max(lookahead,30) (2240, 2408-2413); Sybil co-location is one Counter pass (2669-2671); logdistance widens the candidate window but caps it at radio_cap_max_mult=6x range to keep the search O(local) (256-261, 2705-2715); per-step state pruning + RNG freeing keep long flow runs flat. Verbose heartbeat every ~5% of steps (2959-2961). Hot loop cost is dominated by per-(receiver,broadcast) detector evaluation (2749-2893): ~a dozen float ops + dict ops per pair, all interpreted Python — throughput is roughly tens of thousands of rx-tx pairs per wall-second, fine for the tested scales (arrival_rate 2-5/s, 300 s, grid 6x6 => hundreds of concurrent vehicles) but 10-100x slower than a vectorized/numpy or compiled implementation.

== TIMING / STEP-SIZE ASSUMPTIONS ==
Mock pipeline: fixed step t = step*dt (2531), dt default 1.0 s (cfg 275), UI-permitted range 0.1-5 s (_FIELD_META 1145). Exactly ONE CAM per active vehicle per step (broadcast pre-pass 2544+), i.e. 1 Hz beaconing at default dt — NOT 10 Hz. DoS floods are modeled as msg_count=dos_burst per interval (2579), normalized by freq_max=6 CAMs/interval (360, 2825); congestion threshold chan_capacity=40 in-range CAMs/step (341). Several detectors bake in per-second/per-step semantics: revoke_min_seconds buckets report times with int(tt) (2951); Teleport uses int(t)%4, StopAndGo int(t)%2 (1919, 1936); heading baseline requires (t-prev)<=2*dt (2809); detector_lag_s=1.5 s lagged reference (318, 2795-2803); DENM rate is per-100 s converted to per-step probability denm_rate*dt/window (106-111, 1455-1457). MOSAIC layer: SUMO/MOSAIC step defaults to 0.1 s (SCMS_SIM_STEP, min 50 ms — mapgen.py:121-123 "0.1 s enables up to 10 Hz ETSI CAMs"); the Java beacon app implements REAL ETSI dynamic CAM triggering, T_GenCamMax=1.0 s / T_GenCamMin=0.1 s + movement/heading deltas, so CAM rate varies 1-10 Hz (ScmsBeaconApp.java:40-41, 144-152, comment at 255-259: detection uses a lagged reference precisely so it is CAM-rate independent). MOSAIC radio: SNS SophisticatedAdhocTransmissionModel, singlehopRadius default 709.4 m, SimpleRandomDelay 0.4-2.4 ms (mapgen.py:162-170). MOSAIC seed: scenario_config randomSeed from --seed (gen_scenario.py:102-110); backend master seed SCMS_SEED env or -Dscms.seed default 20260809 (ScmsBackend.java:117-120), per-vehicle sensor RNGs seeded (197), emitRng = seed*104729 (221); backend writes the same trust-separated dataset + manifest.json with data_digest_sha256 at JVM exit (ScmsBackend.java:15, 632-642, per-file sha256 691-696) — mirroring the Python manifest contract.
gaps: Global-stream interleaving is the #1 fragility for any external engine: packet-loss draws, ingest-delay draws and report_prob coins all come from ONE random.Random(cfg.seed) consumed in exact reception order (run.py:1416, 2079, 2657, 2751, 2775, 2888, 2918). If SUMO/TraCI supplies positions, any difference in vehicle count, spawn order, or per-step presence changes the number of broadcasts, hence the number/order of global-stream draws, and every downstream byte changes. External traffic cannot be dropped in without either (a) freezing the trajectory feed into a deterministic, versioned artifact hashed into the manifest, or (b) moving ALL per-event randomness to string-keyed streams keyed on (seed, digest, rx, step) like the shadowing stream already is (run.py:2742-2743).

Vehicle identity mapping: the mock keys every per-vehicle stream on an integer vid assigned in spawn order (f"{seed}:sensor:{vid}"); SUMO vehicle IDs are strings whose insertion order depends on route files and departure resolution. A stable, recorded vid<->SUMO-id mapping is required or all per-vehicle streams shift.

Floating-point provenance: detection decisions (streak gates, thresholds at exactly 1.0, run.py:2884-2885) happen on UNROUNDED floats; rounding to 3 decimals occurs only at serialization. Pure-Python IEEE-double math is cross-platform deterministic, but SUMO (C++), MOSAIC (Java) and any ns-3-class radio sim do not guarantee bitwise-identical floats across versions/platforms/compilers — a 1-ulp position difference near a threshold flips a report, which flips the revocation cascade, which flips the digest. The current contract has no tolerance concept; it is bytes or nothing.

Flow-mode streamed files are written in GENERATION order, not re-sorted (flush_streams run.py:2190-2200, vs the sorted fixed-fleet writer 3064-3073). An external network sim that delivers receptions asynchronously or with nondeterministic tie-breaking changes file byte order even when the row SET is identical.

The manifest replay contract (config_from_dict, run.py:1364-1391) captures only PipelineConfig fields. External-engine inputs — SUMO .net.xml/.rou.xml, MOSAIC scenario_config.json, netgenerate/randomTrips seeds, SUMO/MOSAIC/JDK versions — are not captured in the Python manifest, so a SUMO-fed run would not be replayable from manifest.json alone. (The Java backend writes its own manifest with digests of OUTPUTS, ScmsBackend.java:632-642, but scenario INPUT files are still unhashed.)

Step-size/beacon-rate mismatch: the mock assumes exactly one CAM per vehicle per step and encodes rates as per-step counts (dos_burst, freq_max, chan_capacity, run.py:341,360-361), plus int-second bucketing (revoke_min_seconds via int(tt), run.py:2951) and int(t)%N attack phases (1919,1936). Feeding 10 Hz ETSI-dynamic CAMs (as the MOSAIC layer produces at 0.1 s steps) into this logic without re-normalizing per unit time would distort congestion, DoS detection, and revocation persistence semantics; conversely dt=0.1 in the mock multiplies runtime ~10x with no vectorization to absorb it.

SIGINT handling is process-local and main-thread-only (run.py:2511-2522): with a child SUMO/TraCI process, Ctrl-C on Windows is delivered to the whole console group, so SUMO may die before the finalize path can drain the last step; there is no child-process signal isolation (CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP) or TraCI close-on-abort hook.

No wall-clock performance instrumentation exists (no steps/s, no per-phase timing, no profile notes anywhere in the repo); scaling limits are only inferable from the O() comments. Single-threaded, interpreted, scalar math bounds city-scale realism (thousands of concurrent vehicles at sub-second dt) well below what SUMO+a compiled radio model handles natively.

The determinism test only checks same-machine, same-process byte identity (tests/test_pipeline.py:74-83); there is no cross-platform golden digest, no pinned-environment attestation (Python version, libm) in the manifest, and no per-file record counts to localize a digest mismatch beyond per-file sha256s.
opportunities: Constraint list any external-engine integration MUST respect (the hard contract): (1) SEED: everything derives from the single integer cfg.seed — external seeds (SUMO --seed, netgenerate/randomTrips seed, MOSAIC randomSeed, radio-sim RngRun) must be derived deterministically (e.g. sha256(f"{seed}|sumo")) and recorded in the manifest config, exactly as gen_scenario.py:102-110 already threads --seed into scenario_config. (2) MANIFEST: keep _write_manifest/_data_digest semantics — digest over sorted(rel_path+file sha256) of data files only; wall clock only in build_utc; manifest/viz files excluded; config must round-trip through config_from_dict so --config replays. Extend the config with a content-hash of every external input artifact (net.xml, rou.xml, scenario_config) so replay detects drift. (3) STREAM ISOLATION: new randomness only from string-keyed random.Random(f"{seed}:{label}:{stable_id}") streams; never touch the global rng; gate any new output column/file on an opt-in flag so the default digest is untouched (the pervasive pattern at run.py:2047-2053, 3028-3036). (4) ORDERING: canonicalize every external event batch (sort TraCI vehicle lists by id; sort delivered packets by (step, tx_digest, rx_vid)) before any global-stream draw; keep per-step iteration over sorted vids. (5) SERIALIZATION: rows via ca.canonical_bytes, utf-8, newline="\n", round(...,3) at emission. (6) MEMORY: preserve per-step flush of the big three tables and state pruning; an external feed must be consumable step-by-step (no full-run buffering). (7) CTRL-C: external processes must be launched in their own process group and be stoppable at a step boundary so the _ABORT -> finalize path (run.py:2524-2530, 2973-2975) still writes a valid partial manifest.

Cleanest SUMO/TraCI hook that PRESERVES the contract: replace only Vehicle.true_state()/car_follow() with a trajectory provider, keeping vids, spawn ordering, and all sensor/attack/detection RNG untouched. Two-phase design: phase A runs SUMO once (seeded, fixed step-length, no --scale, single-threaded) and freezes trajectories to a canonical .jsonl (sorted, rounded, sha256-hashed into the manifest as an input artifact); phase B replays that file through the existing loop. This makes SUMO nondeterminism a detectable input-hash change instead of a silent digest break, and keeps Ctrl-C/streaming semantics intact. The custom_network JSON path (road_network="custom", run.py:743-759, validated in validate_config:1054-1056) is the precedent: external map data enters via config, so it is automatically captured in the manifest.

External radio sim hook: the logdistance model already shows the pattern for per-link randomness that is order-independent — random.Random(f"{seed}:shadow:{digest}:{rx}:{step}") (run.py:2742-2743). An external channel model (or an imported loss trace) should be keyed the same way, or delivered as a frozen per-(tx,rx,step) loss table hashed into the manifest; then move the remaining per-packet loss draw (2751) off the global stream onto a link-keyed stream in one flagged, digest-versioned change.

Re-normalize per-step rate semantics before supporting dt<1 or ETSI-dynamic beaconing: express dos_burst/freq_max/chan_capacity per second, bucket revocation evidence by configurable window rather than int(tt) seconds, and replace int(t)%N attack phases with phase accumulators — the Java app already demonstrates rate-independent detection via lagged references (ScmsBeaconApp.java:255-259).

Performance headroom without breaking determinism: (a) add a perf heartbeat (steps/s, rx-tx pairs/s) to the verbose output and manifest counts; (b) vectorize the reception inner product (distance + loss computation) with numpy per step while keeping draw ORDER by precomputing the candidate list then drawing sequentially — or fully migrate per-packet draws to link-keyed streams first, after which vectorization/parallelization is order-free; (c) parallelize massive.py domains across processes (each domain is an independent seeded run whose digest is already recorded per-domain).

Harden reproducibility attestation: record python_version, platform, and implementation in the manifest; add per-file row counts next to sha256s; add a cross-platform golden-digest CI job; for MOSAIC runs, extend the Java manifest (ScmsBackend.java:632-642) to hash scenario INPUT files (map.net.xml, map.rou.xml, scenario_config.json) so both stacks carry a full input+output provenance chain.

Windows Ctrl-C for child engines: launch SUMO/MOSAIC with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, translate the Python-side _ABORT into a graceful traci.close()/MOSAIC stop at the next step boundary, and reuse the existing test seam (PER_STEP_HOOK, tests/test_interrupt.py) to test partial-finalize with a live child process.
notes: Corrections/clarifications vs the task prompt: (1) BSM/CAM is NOT 10 Hz in the Python mock — it is one CAM per vehicle per step, dt default 1.0 s => 1 Hz; 10 Hz exists only in the MOSAIC layer (SCMS_SIM_STEP default 0.1 s, ETSI T_GenCamMin 0.1 s / T_GenCamMax 1.0 s dynamic triggering in ScmsBeaconApp.java:40-41). (2) datagen/models.py is not part of the record schema — it is the deterministic (RNG-free) numpy GBDT benchmark baseline; the record schema is schemas/records.py. (3) No measured performance numbers exist anywhere in the repo; the perf story is purely algorithmic (spatial hashing O(local), streaming, pruning) and single-threaded scalar Python. (4) Determinism does NOT rely on PYTHONHASHSEED: all dict iteration affecting output is over insertion-ordered dicts built in deterministic order or explicitly sorted, and string-keyed random.Random uses the string's sha512-based seeding, which is hash-randomization-independent. (5) The Java/MOSAIC backend mirrors the manifest+digest contract (data_digest_sha256, per-file sha256, seed) but its determinism is env-seeded (SCMS_SEED) and its output digest is computed over Gson-serialized rows, not ca.canonical_bytes — the two stacks' digests are not comparable, only internally reproducible. (6) The osm.py / mapgen city importers feed external map data in via config/scenario files, which is the established deterministic ingestion pattern (content flows through config -> manifest), the model any SUMO/radio integration should copy.
